symbols.note: copied by hand from gatekit symbols system --dll dx11 (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe). Methods with null address were listed by the Toolkit but the tool printed no game address for them. System index variable bg3_dx11.exe+0x60516D8; the game functions using the index are in the Toolkit line of the tool output. The does layer cites EoCServer.dll (Toolkit pseudo-code with real names) wherever bg3_dx11.exe functions were not individually mapped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Five steps run in order each frame: GatherShapeshiftEquipmentRequests, ProcessEquipmentSetRequests, ResolveEquipmentRequests, ProcessInvisibilityEventRequests, CreateEquipmentInteractionRequests.

Adds ShapeshiftEquipmentHistoryComponent to an entity on one path near the start (the guarding condition was not settled). Later, in a loop, two independent tests (not two branches of one choice) each compare a stored entity handle with the current one; on a match the first removes ShapeshiftAddedEquipmentComponent and the second removes ShapeshiftUnequippedEquipmentComponent from that entity. This method removes the two tags; it does not create them. What the compared handles stand for in game terms was not worked out.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe+0x34F7B00 (3475 b, matched to the method at pseudo-code 0.19) read around the two tag type indexes: both go to the same command-buffer helper bg3_dx11.exe+0x400D0A0, which stores only the type index; the one add in the function goes through ComponentFrameStorageAllocRaw with the ShapeshiftEquipmentHistory type. The named counterpart EoCServer.dll+0xFED910 has, at the same two tests, two RemoveComponentUnchecked calls, and one AddComponent earlier. Reviewer, 14 Nov 2026: the first version said these were adds.
